Here's my plan for this year. Let me think through it first.

---

**My thinking, in my own voice:**

My name doesn't matter, what matters is I've been doing this 15 years on these same 19 mu. The land is split — about 12 mu I keep in wheat-maize rotation, and the other 7 mu or so I put in cotton because cotton is where the cash is. My husband works construction in Handan most of the year so he's not around much for field work. My mother-in-law helps me, and my oldest two kids help on weekends and school holidays. Eight mouths in the house, so what we don't sell, we eat.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in October, like always. Right now I need to think about the topdressing and spring water. Then cotton in late April, and maize goes in the minute the wheat combine finishes in June.

For wheat, I do what I always do. One bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, 25 kg bag) per mu before planting, and I already mixed about half a bag of urea in with that. Now when it greens up and starts jointing, I'll go in with another half bag, maybe a bit more, of urea. My neighbor Zhao cut back on her topdress two years ago trying to save money and her wheat came in yellow and short — I'm not doing that. I'll water three times if the spring is dry like it has been. Each watering is 30-40 yuan per mu with the electric pump, so that hurts, but you can't skip it at jointing or you lose the grain.

For maize, the turnaround after wheat is maybe five days. No time to plow, I just broadcast herbicide and plant straight into the stubble. I buy Zhengdan 958 seed from the same dealer in town, about 80 yuan a mu. One bag of compound at planting and a topdress of urea when it gets to my knee. If the rains come in July-August like normal I won't irrigate. If it's dry, one watering.

Cotton is the hardest. More work, more worry. Prices have been okay the last two years but you never know. I plant the Bt seed my sister-in-law uses — it handles the bollworm better so less spraying. Cotton needs hand work all summer: pruning, topping the plants, spraying for aphids and mirids. Come September I'll need to hire two or three women from the village to help pick, at maybe 100 yuan a day. I can pick too but with 7 mu I can't do it alone fast enough.

Money — I have maybe 11,000 yuan to put in across the whole year, counting what I already spent on wheat last fall. If cotton prices drop or the weather turns bad, that's a hard year. But I can't go smaller on fertilizer or the yields drop and then I'm really in trouble. So I spend what I have to and pray for a normal year.
